findings.title: Canonical gateway identity is undecided
findings.details: At verified version dd544b06f81272edfe5af6bde65029aecdee7dcfa24c9f8750191107605007b7, marius-patrik/Andromeda issue #210 delegates selection of the public name, distribution name, Python import namespace, CLI script name, and agent package id to the worker. No authenticated owner-approved values or exact mapping is recorded. Contributor comments and autofix records cannot authorize these semantic product and compatibility choices. The owner must specify every approved identifier before execution.

findings.title: Decision and implementation ownership are mixed
findings.details: The issue is titled as a decision lane but also requires a repository-wide rename, metadata and documentation edits, compatibility handling, and tests. This does not establish one clear execution lane or a deterministic boundary with successor packaging issue #214. The owner must state whether #210 records only the naming decision or also owns implementation, then align its scope, non-goals, deliverables, and successor readiness condition.

findings.title: Compatibility requirements contradict each other
findings.details: One requirement calls for migration aliases where needed, another forbids aliases, bridges, and forwarding shims, and acceptance permits an unspecified compatibility surface. These conditions cannot all be applied deterministically. The owner must classify each legacy distribution, import, CLI, and agent-package identifier as forbidden, temporary with an explicit removal condition, or an approved permanent exception.

findings.title: Planning authority and dependency transitions are unverifiable
findings.details: Issue #210 cites Andromeda-data context/PLAN.md, while trusted canonical state identifies context/TASK.md as the authoritative task board. Although supplied evidence shows #102 closed and #214 open, the contract does not record #102's disposition in the canonical board, the verified relationship to #214, or the exact condition that unblocks #214. The issue must reference canonical planning authority and define those transitions explicitly.

findings.title: Acceptance criteria are not objective or complete
findings.details: The acceptance phrases “one consistent name” and “no undocumented split” do not enumerate the required values and affected surfaces across public identity, distribution metadata, import namespace, CLI entry point, agent package metadata, source paths, documentation, tests, and downstream consumers. Acceptance must define observable checks for every approved mapping, prohibited legacy residue, documented exception, and affected consumer.

findings.title: Change-specific validation and revision evidence are incomplete
findings.details: The issue provides no authoritative focused checks for imports, CLI entry points, built distribution metadata, agent metadata, documentation residue, downstream references, or approved compatibility behavior, and it does not require evidence tied to the implementing revision. The contract must define this coverage and revision-bound evidence. The absence of git diff --check and recursive submodule-status results is not itself a finding because the independent exact-head Validate gate owns those commands.

findings.title: Rollout, failure, and rollback behavior are unspecified
findings.details: Changing distribution, import, CLI, or package identifiers can break consumers, but issue #210 defines no name-availability check, downstream-readiness condition, release ordering, failure behavior, rollback trigger, or removal point for temporary compatibility surfaces. These conditions require owner approval before implementation or release-dependent work can safely proceed.
